chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Slide trombone versus valve and the voice-like quarter tone
summary: The slide trombone can bend between positions like a voice or cello, and he says he never had a lesson and goes by instinct.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: -- (inaudible) as they say. I wanted to ask you about the trombone. It's a different kind of an instrument.
Well, there's two types of trombone. There's a valve and a slide. Which one are you speaking of.
It must be the slide because the valve always seems to me to be just like a trumpet or --

Well I would think it is sort of that way, unless you could -- a lot of people can bend notes with their lips you know. Or either use half valves and you can use half valves and bend the note. But with the trombone -- with the slide trombone, you can go in between the position and get a note like you would call a jazz note. You know, like you'd have a B natural and C. Well there's a quarter sound in between there that you can make with the trombone that you can't do with -- that you can't do with an ordinary horn unless you have a flexi -- very flexible lip. I mean that you can do it -- that is with a trumpet or any other valve instrument --

But with the slide you see -- the slide is more like a human voice. And like you voice -- you can bend it and make different noises. And the same thing goes with the slide. It's more kin to your voice. In other
words, like a cello or a violin, you can -- you've got an inbetween sound you can make. You understand. I think you would call it a quarter tone but I'm not sure.
You know. So that's what I think. I mean -- don't take my word as --

-- as a prayer book. Because I never had a lesson so I don't know. I just go by instinct and of -- of the makings of the horn. I mean the mechanics of music -- I do it my ownself by -- and from things I heard from different people. You know, I mean -- and I kept them in mind. I try to keep an open mind.
Uh-huh. Are those people you're taking about -- were they not necessarily trombone players but who played other instruments --
Yeah. Musicians. Musicians. I can't tell you just who I heard it from, but I have heard it different places and different things.
